clue.text: Lack of medicine for Nobby, it's said

parts.note: a lack of something means there is no amount of it
a dose is a measured amount of medicine

explanation.surface: Someone called Nobby is reportedly going without his medication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nobby, it's said' means a word sounding like Nobby, namely knobby: covered in knobs or nodes. Nobby looks like a nickname but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanists use this word for stems that are knotty, swollen with lumps along their length.

clue.text: Hillmen, seen wandering around the boundary

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit on either side of the boundary word
wandering letters stray from their places, so the word seen is rearranged

parts.note: a pale is a fence or boundary, as in 'beyond the pale'

explanation.surface: Mountain men have been spotted roaming around the perimeter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' turns SEEN into NESE, split as NE...SE; 'around' puts that round PALE.
explanation.definitionFit: The people of the Himalayan kingdom are mountain dwellers.

clue.text: Travelling salesman, a member of the band

definitions.meaning: an old American term for a commercial traveller who drums up trade
the player who keeps the beat on percussion

explanation.definitionFit: A rep who drums up custom, and the musician on the kit.

clue.text: Found in shop, recently-made article from the pottery

indicators.note: the following pieces are found inside the shop word

parts.note: a store is a shop
something recently made is new
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newly made item turns up in a shop selling pottery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found in' puts NEW and A inside STORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dense fired clay ware is a staple product of a potter's kiln.

clue.text: It may preclude an advance, the old boy's story being out of copyright

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil, here with its 's

indicators.note: the story word stands outside the copyright letter, holding it

parts.note: a tale is a story
C is short for copyright, as in the circled C symbol

explanation.surface: A former pupil's tale is now in the public domain, which may halt progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being out of' puts TALE outside C. The surface suggests a lapsed copyright; really the story wraps the copyright sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A hindrance or barrier stands in the way of progress.

clue.text: This used to be the place to change for the Brighton Belle

definitions.text: This used to be the place to change for the Brighton Belle

parts.words: This used to be the place to change for the Brighton Belle
parts.note: the Brighton Belle was a famous London-to-Brighton train, so 'change for' sounds like switching trains; really a belle at the Brighton seaside once changed into her swimsuit in a wheeled hut drawn into the sea

explanation.definitionFit: Victorian bathers changed in a wheeled hut rolled into the waves, a lady's beach changing room.

clue.text: Trudge along quietly holding up a passenger vehicle

indicators.note: in a down answer the letter for quietly sits below, supporting the vehicle

parts.note: a tram is a passenger vehicle on rails
p is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone plods on silently, propping up a bus or tram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding up' places P beneath TRAM in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk heavily and wearily is to trudge on a long hike.

clue.text: Wild cat interrupting dog's turn on the ice

indicators.note: the rearranged letters break into the dog word

parts.note: a chow is a Chinese breed of dog

indicators.note: wild letters run free, so the word cat is rearranged

explanation.surface: A feral cat disrupts a dog as it skates on the ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' makes CTA from CAT; 'interrupting' puts it inside CHOW. 'turn on the ice' is a figure-skating step, not a dog's turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure-skating step that changes edge and direction, named after a Native American people.

clue.text: Volunteer student is employed in otorhinolaryngology

indicators.note: the student and is are put to work inside the medical specialty

parts.note: ENT, ear nose and throat, is the everyday name for this specialty
L for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trainee volunteers in a hospital ear, nose and throat department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employed in' puts L and IS inside ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign up for service of one's own accord, especially in the forces.

clue.text: Stupidly ban tin — material for making bearings

definitions.text: Stupidly ban tin — material for making bearings

indicators.note: something done stupidly is muddled, so the words ban tin and material are rearranged

explanation.surface: It would be foolish to outlaw tin, the stuff used for bearings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stupidly' rearranges BANTIN plus MATERIAL; the alloy is mostly tin, which makes banning tin silly.
explanation.definitionFit: A pewter-like alloy of tin, antimony and copper, used for tableware and bearings.

clue.text: He may be rolling and ruling

definitions.text: He may be rolling and ruling

parts.words: He may be rolling and ruling
parts.note: rolling in money, rich, and governing because of that wealth

explanation.definitionFit: A person whose power stems from wealth; rich people rule.

clue.text: A charge familiar in the Maldives

parts.note: a toll is a charge for using a road or bridge

explanation.surface: A fee that holiday-makers in the Maldives know well.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maldives are made up of coral rings round lagoons, a common sight there.

clue.text: Constant associated with this unit of brightness

definitions.meaning: Constant ... was an English composer and conductor
a unit of luminance in the centimetre-gram-second system

explanation.definitionFit: The composer's surname, and a measure of luminance named after a German physicist.

clue.text: Under which one may travel without mechanical power

definitions.text: Under which one may travel without mechanical power

parts.words: Under which one may travel without mechanical power
parts.note: the momentum that keeps a body moving once the engine stops, as in coasting

explanation.definitionFit: Momentum or driving force keeps things going with no engine.

clue.text: State's second rejection of excellent transport system

indicators.note: rejection sends the excellent mark and the rail network back, reading right to left

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI
RY is short for railway

explanation.surface: The nation's second refusal of a first-class rail network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejection of' turns AIRY round to YRIA after S.
explanation.definitionFit: A Middle Eastern country, a nation with Damascus as capital.

clue.text: Having damaged wing, loth to fly in sunlight

definitions.text: Having damaged wing, loth to fly in sunlight

indicators.note: damaging the words wing and loth knocks their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A bird with an injured wing is reluctant to take off in daylight.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: someone who stays up late shuns daylight.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is active late, like the bird that hunts in the dark.

clue.text: He takes steps to strike repeatedly

definitions.text: He takes steps to strike repeatedly

parts.words: He takes steps to strike repeatedly
parts.note: sounds like someone acting against a target, but describes a performer whose shoes hit the floor again and again

explanation.definitionFit: A performer whose metal-plated shoes beat rhythms on the floor.

clue.text: A young kinsman, the lad under the piano.

indicators.note: in a down answer the lad's word goes below the piano's

parts.note: a grand is a grand piano
a son is a lad, a boy

explanation.surface: A boy relative crawls beneath the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' puts SON below GRAND in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's child is a junior male relative.

clue.text: Investor in charge of a plant

parts.note: an angel backs a theatre show or a start-up with money

explanation.surface: A backer runs a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' reads as a factory in the surface but is a herb.
explanation.definitionFit: An aromatic herb whose stalks are candied for cake decoration.

clue.text: Compose uplifting melody for last movement' of The Planets

indicators.note: in a down answer lifting a word up reads it from bottom to top

parts.note: to pen is to write or compose
a tune is a melody

explanation.surface: Write an inspiring tune for the finale of Holst's suite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' turns PEN to NEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Holst's suite ends with 'the Mystic', named after the eighth planet.

clue.text: Model question

definitions.meaning: someone who sits for an artist or photographer

explanation.definitionFit: One who strikes attitudes for a camera, and a tricky puzzle.

clue.text: Trains porpoises, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: groups of sea mammals or fish swimming together

explanation.definitionFit: To educate someone, and the groups in which whales and fish swim.

clue.text: Does copper represent this in. Chilean currency?

indicators.note: to re-present the letters is to set them out afresh in another order

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A question of whether copper features in Chile's money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represent' (re-present) rearranges DOES with CU; Chile is a big copper producer, so the surface is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: The monetary unit Chile used from 1960 to 1975, also in Portugal.

clue.text: Note written by prime minister about his specious argument

parts.note: so, or soh, is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: the prime minister letters go round the word his

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A memo penned by the premier concerning his dubious case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts PM round HIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A clever but fallacious line of reasoning, as taught by the Greek Sophists.

clue.text: Fair ones, for example, spoken in passages in church

indicators.note: spoken signals that the church word is heard rather than read

parts.note: aisles are the walkways between pews

explanation.surface: Lovely women walk the gangways of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: Fair Isle is one of the Shetland islands, famous for patterned knitwear; 'Fair ones' looks like beautiful people.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair Isle is an island off Scotland, so plural islands include it.

clue.text: Ambassador most of the capital find unenlightened

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the formal style of an ambassador

indicators.note: most of the city's name means its final letter is dropped

parts.note: Athens is the capital of Greece

explanation.surface: An envoy finds most of the city backward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the final S of ATHENS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pagan, lacking religious or moral enlightenment.

clue.text: Posh girl seen around University common

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in Nancy Mitford's U and non-U

indicators.note: the girl's name goes round the university letter

parts.note: Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally

explanation.surface: An upper-class girl is spotted about campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts SAL round U.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary or customary, what normally happens.

clue.text: Dogged'10 ac with evidence of debts?

parts.note: the cross-reference itself, ten across, abbreviated as written in the clue
IOUs, 'I owe you' notes, are written proof of debts

explanation.surface: A rich man pursued with a sheaf of unpaid notes.
explanation.walkthrough: '10 ac' looks like a pointer to 10 across, a plutocrat with debts; read literally it spells TEN AC.
explanation.definitionFit: Persistent, holding on determinedly.

clue.text: Exaggerate merits of surplus merchandise

parts.note: something over is left as a surplus
to merchandise goods is to sell them

explanation.surface: Overhype the worth of excess stock.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise a product or idea beyond what it deserves.

clue.text: Stir caused by adman concealing one's. name

indicators.note: the adman word hides the letters for one's inside it

parts.note: PRO, public relations officer, works in advertising
I is one, with 's giving IS

explanation.surface: A fuss caused by an advertising man hiding his identity.
explanation.walkthrough: Stir is slang for jail, not commotion. 'concealing' puts IS in PRO.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for jail: doing time is 'in stir'.
